verbatim_excerpt:
A 'wide street' is any street 75 feet or more in width. In C5-3, C6-4 or C6-6 Districts, when a front lot line of a zoning lot adjoins a portion of a street whose average width is 75 feet or more and whose minimum width is 65 feet, such portion of a street may be considered a wide street; or when a front lot line adjoins a portion of a street 70 feet or more in width, which is between two portions of a street 75 feet or more in width, and which portion is less than 700 feet in length, such portion may be considered a wide street, and in that case, for the purposes of the height and setback regulations and the measurement of any publicly accessible open area or arcade, the street line shall be considered to be a continuous line connecting the respective street lines of the nearest portions of the street which are 75 feet or more in width.

In Community District 7 in the Borough of Manhattan, the roadways of Broadway between West 94th and West 97th Streets and in Community District 3 in the Borough of Manhattan, the roadways of Allen Street between Rivington and Delancey Streets, which are separated by mapped public park shall each be considered a wide street.

A 'narrow street' is any street less than 75 feet wide.
verbatim_excerpt_composition: Three verbatim paragraphs joined by blank lines: [1] 'street, wide' paragraph 1 (flat 75-ft test + C5-3/C6-4/C6-6 alternate-width + 70-ft connector clause), [2] 'street, wide' paragraph 2 (the two named-street designations), [3] 'street, narrow'. Each paragraph is a byte-exact quote from M4-T018; only the '\n\n' joins are structural. The structured blocks below quote substrings of this excerpt so the content_digest_sha256 (sha256 of this excerpt) covers their source text.

named_street_overrides.verbatim_source_quote: In Community District 7 in the Borough of Manhattan, the roadways of Broadway between West 94th and West 97th Streets and in Community District 3 in the Borough of Manhattan, the roadways of Allen Street between Rivington and Delancey Streets, which are separated by mapped public park shall each be considered a wide street.
named_street_overrides.qualifier_clause: which are separated by mapped public park
named_street_overrides.disposition_reason: The designation is conditioned on the roadways being 'separated by mapped public park' - a physical predicate this TEXTUAL matcher cannot verify (no geometry, no park layer) - and the grammatical scope of that qualifier (Allen row only vs both rows) is an unresolved G6 question (G6-Q1). Conservative refusal: a located row returns INDETERMINATE with full provenance until G6 rules and a map-backed predicate exists. No coding assumption decides the scope.

alternate_width_provisions.verbatim_source_quote: A 'wide street' is any street 75 feet or more in width. In C5-3, C6-4 or C6-6 Districts, when a front lot line of a zoning lot adjoins a portion of a street whose average width is 75 feet or more and whose minimum width is 65 feet, such portion of a street may be considered a wide street; or when a front lot line adjoins a portion of a street 70 feet or more in width, which is between two portions of a street 75 feet or more in width, and which portion is less than 700 feet in length, such portion may be considered a wide street, and in that case, for the purposes of the height and setback regulations and the measurement of any publicly accessible open area or arcade, the street line shall be considered to be a continuous line connecting the respective street lines of the nearest portions of the street which are 75 feet or more in width.
alternate_width_provisions.average_minimum_test: average width of the adjoined street portion >= 75 ft AND minimum width of that portion >= 65 ft
alternate_width_provisions.connector_test: portion width >= 70 ft AND portion length < 700 ft AND it lies between two portions each >= 75 ft wide
alternate_width_provisions.disposition_reason: The clause reads 'may be considered a wide street' (permissive) rather than the declarative 'is any street 75 feet or more in width' - whether it self-executes on a numeric match or requires an affirmative agency determination is an unresolved G6 question (G6-Q2). It also requires portion-level average/minimum width no accepted connector supplies. This TEXTUAL matcher performs NO numeric width computation; it classifies only whether a district is within the provision's C5-3/C6-4/C6-6 vocabulary and returns professional_review_required for those districts.
